cards.text: Paul, the apostle who wrote this letter to the churches of Galatia (Galatians 1:1-2), has been pleading with his friends there (Galatians 4:12-20). Some of them want to be under the law. So Paul stops and asks them a question, and friend, it's the kind of question your boss asks when he KNOWS you didn't read the email.

cards.question: Paul has a question for the Galatians who want to be under the law. What does he ask them?

answers.text: Do you not understand what the law says
Have you kept every part of the law
Who was the first to teach you the law

cards.text: Then Paul goes right to what's written: Abraham, the man God promised to bless (Genesis 12:1-3), had two sons. I had SIX cookie cutter kids on one kitchen counter, and Paul's about to get more lesson out of two sons than I ever got out of all six of mine.

cards.question: Paul says both of Abraham's sons were born to free women.

cards.text: Paul says Abraham's son by the slave woman was born according to the flesh. That slave woman was Hagar, the Egyptian servant of Abraham's wife Sarah (Genesis 16:1).

cards.question: Abraham's son by the slave woman was born according to the flesh, but his son by the free woman was born through the ___.

cards.text: Now Paul says these things serve as illustrations: the two women represent two covenants. Buttercup, one of my cookie cutter kids, would LOVE this guy, because he explains the big stuff with something you can see.

cards.question: Paul says one of the two covenants bears children into slavery. Which mountain does that covenant come from?
Paul says the covenant from Mount Sinai, the one that bears children into slavery, is Hagar.

cards.text: Paul says Hagar stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia AND corresponds to the present-day Jerusalem. A mountain AND a city, friend, and the most I ever stood for was a cookie.

cards.question: Why does Paul say Hagar corresponds to the present-day Jerusalem?

answers.text: She is in slavery with her children
She was buried outside its walls
She once lived inside its gates

cards.text: Paul has just tied Hagar to the present-day Jerusalem. Then he says there's ANOTHER Jerusalem, the Jerusalem above, and friend, I can't even keep track of two oven mitts.

cards.question: Paul says the Jerusalem above is in slavery, just like the present-day Jerusalem.

cards.text: Paul says the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother. Then, like a guy who brings a printout to win the argument, he backs it up with words from the prophet Isaiah (Isaiah 54:1), telling a barren woman who bears no children to rejoice and cry aloud.

cards.question: The words Paul quotes tell the barren woman to rejoice. What reason do they give her?

answers.text: The desolate woman's children outnumber the married woman's
Her husband is on his way home to her
Her fields are full of a great harvest

cards.text: Paul has been talking about Abraham's two sons, Ishmael by Hagar (Genesis 16:15) and Isaac by Sarah (Genesis 21:2-3), and now he turns straight to the Galatians. It's like when the group chat's been talking about everybody else all night and then somebody types your NAME.

cards.question: Paul tells the Galatian believers that, like ___, they are children of promise.

cards.text: Then Paul goes back one more time to how things went between Abraham's two sons, like a guy rewinding the game tape to show you the play AGAIN.

cards.question: Paul says that back then, the son born by the flesh did something to the son born by the Spirit. What did he do?
Paul says the way things went between the two sons back then is the same now.

cards.text: Paul asks, 'But what does the Scripture say?' and friend, when Paul asks THAT, you put your phone down. Then he quotes Genesis 21:10: 'Expel the slave woman and her son…'

cards.question: The Scripture Paul quotes says to expel the slave woman and her son. What reason does it give?

answers.text: Her son will never share in the inheritance
Her son had chosen to live far away
Her son was old enough to live on his own

cards.question: Paul ends by telling the believers that he and they are children of the slave woman.
